Part A – Space Complexity

Exercises 1–5: Identify how much extra memory your solution uses.

1Sum of Two Numbers

Write a Java program to accept two numbers and calculate their sum.

Your task: Identify the variables used and determine the auxiliary space complexity.

What students will learn (ELI10)

After completing this exercise, students should be able to:

  • Learn two ways to reverse the same array and compare their memory use.
  • Approach 1 copies values into a second array: O(n) time and O(n) auxiliary space.
  • Approach 2 swaps the first and last values, then moves inward using two indexes.
  • Understand that in-place swapping uses only a few variables: O(1) auxiliary space.
  • Recognise that both approaches visit a number of elements proportional to n, so both take O(n) time.

Student Submission – Complexity Analysis

Complete this after writing and testing each Java program.

For every exercise, record: Time complexity, auxiliary space complexity, and (where applicable) best, average and worst-case behaviour.

Show analysis checklist
  1. Write the Java program.
  2. Run it with the sample input.
  3. Perform a dry run.
  4. Count important operations or comparisons.
  5. Identify time complexity.
  6. Identify auxiliary space complexity.
